title: America's trade war
hook: Since 2025 the United States has raised tariffs on almost every country. Eight chapters on what changed, who answered how, and who pays.
intro: In 2025 the United States raised its tariffs higher than at any time since the 1930s: first on its neighbours and China, then on almost every country at once, then on whole industries. This series follows it chapter by chapter, and is updated as the story moves.

dates.t: US adds 10% on all goods from China (fentanyl emergency)
25% on Canada and Mexico outside the USMCA; China raised to 20%
'Liberation Day': reciprocal tariffs announced for almost every country
Geneva truce: US–China rates cut to 30% and 10%
Court of International Trade rules the emergency tariffs unlawful
Steel and aluminium tariffs doubled to 50%
New country rates: 15% for the EU, Japan and South Korea; 39% Switzerland
India: 50% including a penalty for buying Russian oil
Trump and Xi meet in Busan: one-year truce
Supreme Court: the emergency law does not allow tariffs (6–3)
Emergency tariffs end; 10% surcharge for 150 days
Surcharge expires; Section 301 'forced labour' tariffs on 60 economies

title: The Roman Empire
hook: From a city on the Tiber to an empire of 5 million km², and two falls a thousand years apart. Chapters on conquest, roads, frontiers and the end.
intro: Rome began as one small city-state in Italy. By AD 117 it ruled every coast of the Mediterranean, from Britain to Egypt. This series follows the Roman state on the map: how it grew by war, how roads tied it together, where it stopped and built walls, how it split in two, and how it fell, in the West in 476 and in the East in 1453. Borders before AD 500 are reconstructions and approximate; each chapter names its sources.
